extracted.intended_audience: mercantile bookkeepers and merchants (historical Italian practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical instructional rules for keeping merchant books: what to record, how to format debits/credits, how to correct errors, how to close and transfer books, and how to manage units/conversions for trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep an orderly quaderno/diario and memoriale
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a day-to-day notebook (quaderno), memoriale and giornale where transactions are recorded promptly and in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record operations as they occur; do not leave items to be written later in scattered places. Use folios and number pages; keep the quaderno tidy and well-kept ("ben tenuto"). Use the giornale/memoriale to ensure you can later transfer systematically to ledgers (libri).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not erase entries; correct with marks and references
rubrics_metrics.description: When an error is made, do not erase or write behind; indicate the mistake and correct it explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark the erroneous entry (for example with a cross/croci) and note the correction in the margin or in the subsequent place; avoid removing folios or writing behind them. If a partition/entry is misplaced, mark it and carry out a proper transfer so the error is traceable rather than obliterated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer and close books by making a bilancio and copying balances
rubrics_metrics.description: When a ledger (libro) or quaderno is full or at period end, prepare a balance (bilancio) and transfer totals and balances into new books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy all credits and debts into the new libro in order, marking the day and reference. The old book should be reduced (ridotto) and the balances verified and recorded in the new book; leave indicia on the cover of the old book. Ensure the copied totals match (parità fra credito e debito).

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep originals of letters, receipts and payments safely and make records
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve original documents (letters, receipts, bills of exchange, payments) and reference them in the books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Store originals in a secure place (secret/safe), make copies and note them in the ledger. For legal letters or family papers, record sender/recipient, date and summary and keep them available. Do not dispose of letters that may be relevant for later proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions for debit (dare) and credit (avere) placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow consistent placement conventions: debtors and debts on one side, creditors and credits on the other; keep parity and alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record 'debiti' on the left and 'crediti' on the right (or follow the local practice but be consistent). Make corresponding entries so that totals balance. When transferring a credit to the debit side (or vice versa) mark the movement and date to preserve audit trail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record full particulars: date, name, commodity, quantity, price, and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry should include the date, the counterparty's name, the article/merchandise, quantity, price and payment terms (e.g., sold 'a termine').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether the sale was cash or at term, the maturity date, and to whom the credit or debit pertains. For bills or transfers, note the mode of payment and any signatures or obligations. This enables clear identification of each obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record consignments, term sales and multi-stage contracts clearly (debtor/creditor assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: When goods are sold on credit, consigned, or part of a multi-contract arrangement, record which party is debtor and which is creditor and the specific terms of each stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a merchandise sale is to be paid at a later term, note the debtor (the buyer) and the credit (the seller) explicitly; for chains of agreements, record each step (first contract, then a subsequent contract making someone else debtor/creditor). Use clear labels so later transfers or assignments are traceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use memorandum entries for small or ephemeral items
rubrics_metrics.description: Very small-value items or transient matters may be kept as a memorandum rather than in the main ledger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor items that are not worth recording in the formal libro may be noted in a separate memo or marginal note (ricordo), but still kept so that they can be admitted into accounts if needed later. Avoid cluttering the main book with trivial items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an alphabetical/indexed system to locate entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an index (alphabet) or marking system to facilitate finding specific entries or counterparties in the books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place letters of the alphabet at the relevant places, or otherwise mark pages to make searching quick ("l’alfabeto ognuno al tuo luogo"). Using an index or labelled folios speeds retrieval of a name or transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep conversion tables and standardized measures for markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain tables of weights, measures and money conversions specific to different markets and cities used in trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because markets use differing local units and coinages, keep a reference table listing measures, weights, and the value conversions for places (the page contains a long list of city-specific weights/values). Use these consistently when entering prices and quantities to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use separate books for different transaction types
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep different ledgers/books for different purposes (e.g., giornale, libro dei crediti, libro dei debiti), rather than recording everything in one volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mixing different categories in a single book: have dedicated books for receipts, for credits, for merchandise records etc., and transfer summarized totals between books systematically. This improves clarity and auditing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure totals of debits and credits match; reconcile discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: At closing or when reconciling, totals on debit and credit sides must correspond; if not, investigate and correct rather than hide mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an imbalance arises, mark the erroneous entry and make appropriate corrective entries in the next folio/book; use reduction (riduzione) and reconciliation (bilancio) steps to find and fix the cause. Never obscure mismatches—document corrections clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record lost, sold, donated or disposed goods in the margin
rubrics_metrics.description: Items removed from inventory (sold, lost, given away) should be noted in the margin beside the original entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For items that have been sold, donated or lost, write a marginal note indicating the disposition so the inventory/accounting reflects the change without destroying the original entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify payment mode and dates for creditor/debtor entries
rubrics_metrics.description: When recording debts or credits, include how payment is to be made and the exact dates or terms (scadenza), and mark payments when they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the day and payment method for each debt or credit. When a payment is made, note it on the same day and update the ledger so the status (paid/unpaid) is evident. For transferable bills, note any endorsements or transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standardized abbreviations/symbols for currencies and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt consistent abbreviations for lire, soldi, denari, ducati, fiorini, weights and other units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual lists abbreviations (e.g., lire, soldi, danari, ducati, fiorini) and recommended symbols to avoid ambiguity. Use these conventions throughout to keep entries concise and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mix temporary informal loans with formal ledger entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Small personal loans or fleeting favors between friends may be kept as reminders but should not be immediately entered in the formal merchant book unless material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For small personal loans or brief favors, keep a short memorandum; if they become significant or are to be collected, then make formal ledger entries. This keeps commercial books focused on trade-related obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reducing or consolidating books, preserve an audit trail
rubrics_metrics.description: When copying or reducing an old libro into a new volume, keep references to the original entries and dates so records remain verifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the original folio/page references when transferring entries; the old book should be kept with an indication of its being carried forward. If the old book is cancelled or closed, the closure should be evident (e.g., noting the cover) and the new book should include the copied totals and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle multi-party or conditional obligations explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: For transactions involving commissions, consignments, barter, or conditional promises, document the exact commitments, who is obliged, and under what conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the terms (conditionati), quantities, who is sending goods, who holds them, and any return expectations. For barter or exchange of goods between parties, record each side as credit/debit with the agreed valuation and terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep separate records for stores/stock in the bottega
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the goods physically present in the shop or warehouse separately from book entries, noting sales, consignments and stock reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory items that are kept in the shop should be entered in a shop register or memo; when sold or consumed, mark them in the inventory record and, if material, in the accounts. Use marginal notations for items sold or removed from stock.
